# μForge.io

> μForge.io is an open-source development platform for innovative semiconductor solutions, starting with the SF32 family of ultra-low-power AIoT microcontrollers from SiFli. It brings together chip and module documentation, development-board references, SDK/platform guides, and production-ready hardware design guides for developers building connected, intelligent, energy-efficient embedded products.

Primary audience: hardware engineers, PCB designers, firmware/software engineers, and product engineers selecting parts or designing hardware around the SF32 family. Content favors practical engineering detail (part selection, pin assignments, electrical specs, PCB layout rules, integration risk) over marketing language.

Only the pages listed below are published on this site. Internal working notes, process documentation, and authoring templates are excluded from this domain entirely and are not part of the public content set.

## Getting Started

- [Getting Started Overview](https://uForge.io/getting-started/): Comparison of SF32 software paths — SiFli-SDK, CodeKit, Zephyr, Arduino, and MicroPython — and which are production-ready today.
- [Getting Started with SiFli-SDK](https://uForge.io/getting-started/sifli/getting-started-sifli-sdk/): From an unboxed SF32 dev board to a running hello_world example over UART using the official RT-Thread-based SDK.
- [Getting Started with SiFli CodeKit](https://uForge.io/getting-started/sifli/getting-started-sifli-codekit/): Using the SiFli CodeKit VS Code extension to install SDK tools, select a board, build, flash, and monitor.
- [Getting Started with Zephyr](https://uForge.io/getting-started/zephyr/getting-started-zephyr-upstream/): Using OpenSiFli's downstream Zephyr tree and SiFli HAL module for SF32LB52.
- [Getting Started with Arduino](https://uForge.io/getting-started/arduino/getting-started-arduino/): Using OpenSiFli's beta Zephyr-based Arduino core for the SF32LB52 DevKit LCD.
- [MicroPython Status](https://uForge.io/getting-started/micropython/getting-started-micropython/): Readiness checklist for MicroPython on SF32; not yet a supported path pending official firmware images.
- [Getting Started with Rust](https://uForge.io/getting-started/rust/getting-started-rust/): First evaluation of OpenSiFli sifli-rs on SF32LB52 — install the Rust target, build the unmodified Blinky example, configure sftool, and retain an SDK recovery path.

## Hardware — Task Hubs

- [SF32 Products](https://uForge.io/sf32-products/): Start here to explore SF32 hardware, plan a product, choose a chip, module, or development board, reuse a reference design, and prepare a production design.
- [Hardware](https://uForge.io/hardware/): Reuse an SF32 reference baseline or implement a selected device, then prepare the design for production.
- [Plan a Product](https://uForge.io/sf32-products/family/product-planning/): End-to-end path from requirements and device selection through board validation and production design.
- [Reference Designs](https://uForge.io/hardware/reference-designs/reference-designs/): Reference-design journeys for μForge — compare reproducible hardware and software validation paths, then follow the one closest to your product.
- [Connected Wearable Reference-Design Journey](https://uForge.io/hardware/reference-designs/connected-wearable-journey/): A practical SF32 reference-design journey from SF32LB52 development-board validation to a custom connected wearable hardware and firmware release plan.
- [SF32 Product Selector](https://uForge.io/sf32-products/product-selector/): Select an SF32 chip or module by product constraints, integration level, and software-validation path.
- [Design for Production](https://uForge.io/hardware/design-for-production/): Production-design path for SF32 hardware design guides, checklists, interface definitions, approved components, and EDA libraries.

## Hardware — Chips

- [SF32 Family Overview](https://uForge.io/sf32-products/family/SF32_family/): Portfolio overview of the SF32LB5xx series of highly integrated, ultra-low-power 32-bit microcontrollers for battery-powered AIoT and wearable applications.
- [SF32 Naming Rule](https://uForge.io/sf32-products/family/SF32_namingrule/): How to read SF32 part numbers, including the numeric/alphabetic variant placeholders used across chip families.
- [SF32LB52x Introduction](https://uForge.io/sf32-products/chips/SF32LB52x/): Cost-optimized dual-core Arm Cortex-M33 AIoT MCU with Bluetooth, ePicasso graphics, and low power for smart wearables.
- [SF32LB52x Hardware Design Guide](https://uForge.io/hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB52x_hardware_design_guide/): Device overview, design flow, and links to the schematic, PCB layout, and review/reference pages for SF32LB52x designs.
- [SF32LB52x Hardware Design Guide — Schematic Design Guidelines: Minimum System, Power & Clock](https://uForge.io/hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB52x_schematic_design/): Schematic design guidelines for the SF32LB52x MCU: minimum system design, power system, and clock generation.
- [SF32LB52x Hardware Design Guide — RF & User Interfaces](https://uForge.io/hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB52x_schematic_rf_interfaces/): RF and user-interface schematic design guidelines for the SF32LB52x MCU: antenna matching, display, audio, buttons, and vibration motor.
- [SF32LB52x Hardware Design Guide — Storage & Manufacturing](https://uForge.io/hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB52x_schematic_storage_mfg/): Storage, connectivity, and manufacturing-access schematic design guidelines for the SF32LB52x MCU: boot storage, sensors, debug/download interface, and production flashing.
- [SF32LB52x Hardware Design Guide — Schematic Checklist](https://uForge.io/hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB52x_schematic_checklist/): Item-by-item schematic review checklist for the SF32LB52x MCU, covering package, power, clock, RF, storage, display, and manufacturing checks.
- [SF32LB52x Hardware Design Guide — PCB Layout Guidelines](https://uForge.io/hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB52x_pcb_layout/): PCB layout guidelines for the SF32LB52x MCU: footprint, stack-up, routing, power, and EMI/ESD.
- [SF32LB52x Hardware Design Guide — PCB Layout Checklist](https://uForge.io/hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB52x_pcb_layout_checklist/): Item-by-item PCB layout review checklist for the SF32LB52x MCU, covering package, routing, power, and grounding checks.
- [SF32LB52x Hardware Design Guide — Design Review Checklist and References](https://uForge.io/hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB52x_review_and_reference/): Design review checklist, related documents and references, appendices, and revision history for the SF32LB52x hardware design guide.
- [SF32LB55x Introduction](https://uForge.io/sf32-products/chips/SF32LB55x/): Mainstream ultra-low-power AIoT MCU with big.LITTLE dual-core architecture and BLE connectivity for wearables.
- [SF32LB55x Hardware Design Guide](https://uForge.io/hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB55x_hardware_design_guide/): Device overview, design flow, and links to the schematic, PCB layout, and review/reference pages for SF32LB55x designs.
- [SF32LB55x Hardware Design Guide — Schematic Design Guidelines](https://uForge.io/hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB55x_schematic_design/): Schematic design guidelines for the SF32LB55x MCU: power system, boot mode, clock generation, RF, storage interfaces, display and touch interfaces, and wake/GPADC/manufacturing interfaces.
- [SF32LB55x Hardware Design Guide — Schematic Checklist](https://uForge.io/hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB55x_schematic_checklist/): Item-by-item schematic review checklist for the SF32LB55x MCU, covering power, clock, RF, storage, display, and manufacturing checks.
- [SF32LB55x Hardware Design Guide — PCB Layout Guidelines](https://uForge.io/hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB55x_pcb_layout/): PCB layout guidelines for the SF32LB55x MCU: footprint, stack-up, general PCB rules, interface routing, and the item-by-item PCB layout checklist.
- [SF32LB55x Hardware Design Guide — Design Review Checklist and References](https://uForge.io/hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB55x_review_and_reference/): Design review checklist, related documents and references, appendices, and revision history for the SF32LB55x hardware design guide.
- [SF32LB56x Introduction](https://uForge.io/sf32-products/chips/SF32LB56x/): Advanced AIoT MCU with dual-mode Bluetooth, big.LITTLE dual-core architecture, and rich graphics, audio, and memory options.
- [SF32LB56x Hardware Design Guide](https://uForge.io/hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB56x_hardware_design_guide/): Device overview, design flow, and links to the schematic, PCB layout, and review/reference pages for SF32LB56x designs.

- [SF32LB56x Hardware Design Guide — Schematic Checklist](https://uForge.io/hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB56x_schematic_checklist/): Item-by-item schematic review checklist for the SF32LB56x MCU, covering power, clock, RF, storage, display, and manufacturing checks.
- [SF32LB56x Hardware Design Guide — PCB Layout Guidelines](https://uForge.io/hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB56x_pcb_layout/): PCB layout guidelines for the SF32LB56x MCU: footprint, stack-up, critical routing, and the item-by-item PCB layout checklist.

- [SF32LB58x Introduction](https://uForge.io/sf32-products/chips/SF32LB58x/): Flagship AIoT MCU with heterogeneous triple-core architecture, dual-mode Bluetooth, large memory, and rich display and audio I/O.
- [SF32LB58x Hardware Design Guide](https://uForge.io/hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB58x_hardware_design_guide/): Device overview, design flow, and links to the schematic, PCB layout, and review/reference pages for SF32LB58x designs.

- [SF32LB58x Hardware Design Guide — Schematic Checklist](https://uForge.io/hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB58x_schematic_checklist/): Item-by-item schematic review checklist for the SF32LB58x MCU, covering power, clock, RF, storage, display, and manufacturing checks.
- [SF32LB58x Hardware Design Guide — PCB Layout Guidelines](https://uForge.io/hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB58x_pcb_layout/): PCB layout guidelines for the SF32LB58x MCU: package footprint, stack-up, fanout, and routing guidance for clock, RF, audio, USB, SDIO, DSI, and power.
- [SF32LB58x Hardware Design Guide — PCB Layout Checklist](https://uForge.io/hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB58x_pcb_layout_checklist/): Item-by-item PCB layout review checklist for the SF32LB58x MCU, covering package, power, clock, RF, audio, high-speed signals, and stack-up checks.

## Hardware — Modules

- [Module Interface Standards](https://uForge.io/hardware/m2-modules/interface-standards-overview/): μForge M2 module-interface conventions — use the naming rules for stable terminology and treat the pin-level interface definition as a draft to validate before carrier-board commitment.
- [M2 Interface Naming Rules](<https://uForge.io/hardware/m2-modules/M2 Interface Naming Rules/>): The mandatory base module interface identifier implemented by every μForge module; electrical/mechanical pinout is still in development.
- [M2 Interface Definition](https://uForge.io/hardware/m2-modules/M2-interface-definition/): Draft M2 interface definition — connector, pinout, and electrical limits — a working proposal, not yet a released standard.
- [SF32LB52-MOD-1 Introduction](https://uForge.io/sf32-products/modules/SF32LB52-MOD-1/): Certified Bluetooth 6.3 MCU module built on SF32LB525UC6, reducing RF certification and layout risk for wearable products.
- [SF32LB52-MOD-1 Hardware Design Guide](https://uForge.io/hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB52-MOD-1_hardware_design_guide/): Power, interfaces, and PCB integration guidance for the SF32LB52-MOD-1 module.
- [SF32LB56-MOD Introduction](https://uForge.io/sf32-products/modules/SF32LB56-MOD/): General-purpose Bluetooth 6.3 MCU module family based on SF32LB56xV, with graphics, audio, and reduced RF layout risk.
- [SF32LB56-MOD Hardware Design Guide](https://uForge.io/hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB56-MOD_hardware_design_guide/): Power, interfaces, and PCB integration guidance for the SF32LB56-MOD module.
- [SF32LB58-MOD Introduction](https://uForge.io/sf32-products/modules/SF32LB58-MOD/): Certified flagship Bluetooth MCU module built on SF32LB586VDD36, with graphics, storage, and reduced RF/BGA layout risk.
- [SF32LB58-MOD Hardware Design Guide](https://uForge.io/hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB58-MOD_hardware_design_guide/): Power, interfaces, and PCB integration guidance for the SF32LB58-MOD module.

## Hardware — Development Boards

- [SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD](https://uForge.io/sf32-products/devkits/SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD/): SF32LB52-based development board with LCD, audio amplifier, TF-card slot, and battery charger for evaluation and firmware bring-up.
- [SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3](https://uForge.io/sf32-products/devkits/SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3/): SF32LB52-based 3.3 V core development board with maximum pin breakout for direct signal access.
- [SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano](https://uForge.io/sf32-products/devkits/SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano/): Smallest SF32LB52-based development board, for size-constrained product prototyping.
- [SF32LB52-DevKit-ULP](https://uForge.io/sf32-products/devkits/SF32LB52-DevKit-ULP/): Ultra-low-power-focused SF32LB52-based development board for battery-life evaluation.
- [SF32LB56-DevKit-LCD](https://uForge.io/sf32-products/devkits/SF32LB56-DevKit-LCD/): SF32LB56-DevKit-LCD development board — an SF32LB56xV module-based display, audio, storage, and peripheral-development platform.
- [SF32LB58-DevKit-LCD](https://uForge.io/sf32-products/devkits/SF32LB58-DevKit-LCD/): SF32LB58-based development board with LCD for flagship-tier evaluation and firmware bring-up.

## Hardware — Other Resources

- [Components and CAD Libraries](https://uForge.io/hardware/cad-components/components-and-cad-libraries/): Start an SF32 production design with the right component qualifications and official CAD data, then complete the BOM-to-layout review in the correct order.
- [SiFli Approved Vendor List](https://uForge.io/hardware/cad-components/sifli-approved-vendor-list/): SiFli's qualification record for passive components and second-source ICs commonly designed around SF32 devices — crystals, buck inductors, Flash, LCD drivers, and touch controllers.
- [EDA Tool Libraries](https://uForge.io/hardware/cad-components/eda-tool-libraries/): Schematic-symbol and PCB-footprint libraries for SF32 chips and modules, for schematic capture and PCB layout.

## Develop

- [Develop Overview](https://uForge.io/develop/): Entry point for firmware developers building, flashing, debugging, updating, and shipping software on SF32 devices.
- [Develop Overview](https://uForge.io/develop/): Canonical SF32 software-support matrix and development-path guide — compare board and SoC coverage for SiFli-SDK, CodeKit, Zephyr, Arduino, Rust, and MicroPython before choosing a development path.
- [SiFli-SDK Platform Overview](https://uForge.io/develop/platforms/sifli-sdk/overview/): How to use SiFli-SDK day to day once the toolchain works — the reference RT-Thread-based path for SF32 firmware.
- [Build, Flash, Monitor](https://uForge.io/develop/platforms/sifli-sdk/build-flash-monitor/): The daily SiFli-SDK loop — activate the environment, build with scons, flash the board, and watch logs.
- [Board Configuration](https://uForge.io/develop/platforms/sifli-sdk/board-configuration/): How the --board value selects the board support package controlling flash layout, PSRAM, pins, display, audio, clocking, and power rails.
- [Components and sf_pkg](https://uForge.io/develop/platforms/sifli-sdk/components/): SiFli's reusable middleware, driver, and component ecosystem for firmware that grows beyond a copied example.
- [Debugging and Diagnostics](https://uForge.io/develop/platforms/sifli-sdk/debugging-diagnostics/): Serial logs, crash dumps, trace capture, and shell commands for debugging SF32 firmware.
- [SDK Application Notes](https://uForge.io/develop/platforms/sifli-sdk/sdk-application-notes/): A task-oriented, source-linked reading path through the SiFli-SDK usage guides for SF32 development.
- [Sample with GPADC](https://uForge.io/develop/platforms/sifli-sdk/application-notes/adc-sampling/): Use the general-purpose ADC (GPADC) across SF32LB52x, SF32LB55x, SF32LB56x, SF32LB57x, and SF32LB58x: electrical limits, pad mapping, device access, and calibration.
- [Integrate and Read Sensors](https://uForge.io/develop/platforms/sifli-sdk/application-notes/sensor-integration/): Add a sensor to SiFli-SDK, connect it through RT-Thread, register the device, and validate it from the FinSH shell.
- [Use External Flash](https://uForge.io/develop/platforms/sifli-sdk/application-notes/external-flash/): Configure, access, mount, and port external NOR Flash, NAND Flash, and PSRAM with SiFli-SDK.
- [Configure the Watchdog](https://uForge.io/develop/platforms/sifli-sdk/application-notes/watchdog/): Enable, feed, and validate the SF32 HCPU and LCPU watchdog paths with SiFli-SDK.
- [Compress Graphics Assets with EZIP](https://uForge.io/develop/platforms/sifli-sdk/application-notes/ezip-image-assets/): Convert PNG assets to EZIP, PIXEL, LVGL C, and hardware-decompressible GZIP formats with SiFli-SDK.
- [Configure and Measure Low Power](https://uForge.io/develop/platforms/sifli-sdk/application-notes/low-power-measurement/): Configure SiFli-SDK power modes, wake sources, clocks, and board-level current measurements.
- [Capture Logs and Analyze Crashes](https://uForge.io/develop/platforms/sifli-sdk/application-notes/crash-analysis/): Capture matching logs and memory, restore a crash context, and analyze assertions or hard faults with SiFli-SDK tools.
- [Run SiFli SDK RF Tests](https://uForge.io/develop/platforms/sifli-sdk/application-notes/rf-performance-tests/): Choose the correct Bluetooth RF test mode, control path, and measurement equipment.
- [Run Bluetooth Signaling Tests](https://uForge.io/develop/platforms/sifli-sdk/application-notes/bluetooth-signalling-tests/): Connect SF32 DUTs to a Bluetooth tester and perform BLE or Classic Bluetooth signaling measurements.
- [Run Bluetooth Single-Item RF Tests](https://uForge.io/develop/platforms/sifli-sdk/application-notes/bluetooth-single-tone-tests/): Use SiFli_RfTool to control BLE or Classic Bluetooth RF one operation at a time for board tuning and pre-compliance work.
- [CodeKit](https://uForge.io/develop/tools/codekit/): The VS Code extension workflow for SiFli-SDK setup, project creation, build, flash, and monitor.
- [Zephyr Platform Overview](https://uForge.io/develop/platforms/zephyr/overview/): OpenSiFli's downstream Zephyr tree, SiFli HAL integration, and SF32LB52 board support.
- [Arduino Platform Overview](https://uForge.io/develop/platforms/arduino/overview/): OpenSiFli's beta Zephyr-based Arduino core for SF32LB52.
- [MicroPython Platform Status](https://uForge.io/develop/platforms/micropython/status/): Current state of MicroPython support on SF32 — no official port or firmware image yet.
- [Rust Platform Overview](https://uForge.io/develop/platforms/rust/overview/): OpenSiFli's work-in-progress Rust HAL, PAC, and flash-table crates for SF32.
- [Development Tools](https://uForge.io/develop/tools/): Map of download tools, serial monitors, crash analysis, trace capture, image conversion, and RF/audio tuning utilities for SF32 firmware development.
- [Firmware Topics](https://uForge.io/develop/firmware-topics/): Cross-platform firmware mechanics — boot layout, partition tables, OTA/DFU, USB, power management, logging, and crash analysis.
- [Partition Tables](https://uForge.io/develop/firmware-topics/partition-tables/): How flash is divided among firmware, boot data, filesystems, OTA images, and product data.
- [OTA and DFU](https://uForge.io/develop/firmware-topics/ota-dfu/): Update-architecture decisions — transport, signing, rollback, and interrupted-update recovery.
- [USB and CherryUSB](https://uForge.io/develop/firmware-topics/usb-cherryusb/): USB as a software stack on SF32 — descriptors, host OS behavior, power, and factory tooling considerations.
- [Power Management](https://uForge.io/develop/firmware-topics/power-management/): Turning a working prototype into a wearable-ready product via clocking, sleep modes, display, Bluetooth interval, and sensor-wake tuning.
- [Logging and Crash Analysis](https://uForge.io/develop/firmware-topics/logging-crash-analysis/): Designing logging and crash-dump capture before the first field test, not after a device fails.
- [Examples](https://uForge.io/develop/examples/): Why and how to start SF32 firmware from a close working example instead of building each subsystem from scratch.

## Learn

- [Learn Overview](https://uForge.io/learn/): Find SF32 guidance by design question: graphics, Bluetooth, AI, audio, low power, and architecture.
- [Architecture Overview](https://uForge.io/learn/architecture/overview/): Choose the right SF32 processor or hardware-offload detail for an application workload.
- [STAR-MC1](https://uForge.io/learn/architecture/star-mc1/): Arm China's enhanced Cortex-M33 implementation used as the application processor across the SF32 family.
- [PSRAM vs. Other Embedded Memory Types](https://uForge.io/learn/architecture/psram-and-memory-types/): PSRAM versus SRAM, DRAM, RRAM, and MRAM, with embedded buffer-placement and SF32 memory-hierarchy guidance.
- [PTM Parallel Task Machine](https://uForge.io/learn/architecture/ptm-parallel-task-machine/): SF32LB57x's programmable peripheral task engine for timing-sensitive, custom, or small offload work.
- [Graphics Overview](https://uForge.io/learn/graphics/overview/): Display-resource, composition, framebuffer-compression, and panel-output decisions for SF32 UIs.
- [ePicasso 2D / 2.5D Graphics Engine](https://uForge.io/learn/graphics/epicasso-gpu/): How SiFli's ePicasso 2D/2.5D graphics engine accelerates embedded UI rendering on SF32, and how it works with LVGL, memory, and the display controller.
- [eZip Lossless Compression and Hardware Decoding](https://uForge.io/learn/graphics/ezip/): How SiFli eZip and eZip-A reduce embedded UI asset storage, memory bandwidth, and CPU decode work on supported SF32 devices.
- [TurboPixel Framebuffer Compression](https://uForge.io/learn/graphics/turbopixel/): How TurboPixel uses fixed-ratio lossy framebuffer compression to reduce PSRAM capacity and bandwidth on supported SF32 devices.
- [Display Controller](https://uForge.io/learn/graphics/display-controller/): How the SF32 display controller transfers prepared pixels to a panel, including interface selection, flush paths, partial refresh, and panel bring-up.
- [LVGL SDK Examples](https://uForge.io/learn/graphics/lvgl-sdk-examples/): Choose the right SiFli-SDK LVGL example for UI bring-up, widgets, design tools, compressed assets, animation, media, and wearable interfaces.
- [Bluetooth Overview](https://uForge.io/learn/bluetooth/overview/): BLE, dual-mode Bluetooth, profiles, security, coexistence, and device selection.
- [Bluetooth Processor](https://uForge.io/learn/bluetooth/processor/): How SF32's dedicated Bluetooth processor offloads radio timing and link control from the application CPU, enabling low-power always-connected products.
- [Bluetooth PAN](https://uForge.io/learn/bluetooth/pan/): Bluetooth PAN on SF32 — how BNEP, NAP, GN, and PANU roles work, when to use a phone-tethered PAN link instead of adding Wi-Fi, and how to bring up SiFli-SDK's PAN example, including PAN-based OTA delivery.
- [Bluetooth SDK Examples](https://uForge.io/learn/bluetooth/bluetooth-sdk-examples/): Choose the right SiFli-SDK Bluetooth example for BLE services, Classic Bluetooth profiles, phone integration, OTA, data transfer, or LE Audio broadcast.
- [Bluetooth Low-Power Profiling](https://uForge.io/learn/bluetooth/bluetooth-low-power-profiling/): A practical method to measure BLE, Classic Bluetooth, and dual-mode Bluetooth power consumption on an SF32 device, attribute the trace to firmware behavior, and turn the result into a daily-use energy budget.
- [Bluetooth AT Command Reference](https://uForge.io/learn/bluetooth/at-command-reference/): Complete AT command reference for the SF32LB57 dual-mode Bluetooth AT command module (SIFLI_AT): command framing, system and device, address and identity, operating mode and visibility, pairing and security, serial port and events, connection management, data transfer, and custom GATT commands, plus unsolicited events (URCs) and PDU-format commands.
- [AI Overview](https://uForge.io/learn/ai/overview/): Product-level planning for on-device AI, including model fit, memory, latency, and power.
- [AI Accelerator](https://uForge.io/learn/ai/accelerator/): How the SF32 AI accelerator hardware speeds up on-device machine learning and signal processing, and why edge AI matters for wearables and AIoT products.
- [Audio Overview](https://uForge.io/learn/audio/overview/): Local audio architecture, interfaces, buffering, Audio Server middleware, and power tradeoffs.
- [Audio Server and Buffering](https://uForge.io/learn/audio/audio-server-buffering/): Practical SF32 Audio Server and DMA-buffering guidance for glitch-free playback, recording, and coexistence with Bluetooth and graphics.
- [Audio SDK Examples](https://uForge.io/learn/audio/audio-sdk-examples/): Choose the right SiFli-SDK audio example for PDM microphone capture, recording, playback, codecs, storage, and mixing.
- [Low-Power Overview](https://uForge.io/learn/low-power/overview/): System-level low-power design and measured battery-life validation.
- [Power Measurement and Validation](https://uForge.io/learn/low-power/measurement-and-validation/): A repeatable SF32 power-measurement and validation workflow for active, connected-idle, display-off, sleep, and wake scenarios.
- [Low-Power SDK Examples](https://uForge.io/learn/low-power/low-power-sdk-examples/): Choose the right SiFli-SDK power-management example for sleep, wake sources, GPIO, CPU, Bluetooth, displays, UI, and wearable power scenarios.
- [Battery Capacity Calculation](https://uForge.io/learn/low-power/battery-capacity-calculation/): Estimate battery percentage on SF32 products from battery voltage using the SiFli-SDK battery calculator, matched charge/discharge curves, charger-state detection, and multi-stage filtering.
- [Smartwatch Power Profiling](https://uForge.io/learn/low-power/smartwatch-power-profiling/): Build and validate a smartwatch battery-life model from daily usage scenarios, then use the result to prioritize low-power work.

## Projects

- [Projects](https://uForge.io/projects/): End-to-end μForge projects that combine selected hardware, a software baseline, validation evidence, and a production handoff.
- [SF32 Xiaozhi Voice Assistant](https://uForge.io/projects/sf32-xiaozhi/): A complete product-development path for the open-source Xiaozhi voice assistant on SF32LB52 — board bring-up, Bluetooth PAN provisioning, cloud voice interaction, customization, OTA, validation, and production handoff.
- [Arduboy2 on SiFli](https://uForge.io/projects/arduboy2-sifli/): A reproducible path for evaluating OpenSiFli's Arduboy2 port, validating the SF32 display/input/audio boundary, and deciding whether a game-oriented product adaptation is ready for deeper design work.
- [SF32 BLE Talkback](https://uForge.io/projects/sf32-ble-talkback/): A product-development path for reproducing and qualifying multi-device BLE push-to-talk with SF32LB52-DevKit-ULP and OpenSiFli Talkback.
- [SF32 EPD Reader](https://uForge.io/projects/sf32-epd-reader/): A product-development path for reproducing and qualifying the OpenSiFli EPD Reader on SF32-OED-EPD hardware.
- [SuperKey](https://uForge.io/projects/superkey/): An engineering path for the SF32LB52-based SuperKey with three displays, USB HID/CDC, and a desktop companion: reproduce, validate communications and recovery, adapt deliberately, and hand off to product design.
- [Radiation Monitor](https://uForge.io/projects/radiation-monitor/): An SF32LB52-based 2.4 GHz energy viewer: reproduce Radiation Monitor, verify its 79-point scan, RSSI smoothing, and history playback, then define calibration and product-review boundaries.
- [Pocket Pi](https://uForge.io/projects/pocket-pi/): A reproducible Pocket Pi engineering path: validate NES emulation, 320 × 240 display, AW9523 input, audio, ROM filesystems, and save-state recovery on SF32LB52.
- [LilyGO T-Display-SF32](https://uForge.io/projects/lilygo-t-display-sf32/): A product-engineering path for LilyGO's third-party T-Display-SF32 platform: establish the vendor baseline, validate its display, peripherals, power behavior, and recovery, reproduce the SiFli-SDK build, and adapt it deliberately.
- [ZMK on SF32](https://uForge.io/projects/zmk-sf32/): An engineering path for OpenSiFli's ZMK port on SF32LB52: reproduce the Urchin split-keyboard baseline, validate USB, BLE, settings, and recovery, then adapt the keymap or hardware deliberately.

## Getting Started — Tutorials

- [Tutorials Overview](https://uForge.io/getting-started/tutorials/overview/): Recommended SF32 learning sequence, prerequisites, hardware setup, and the next destination after each stage.
- [Beginner Tutorials](https://uForge.io/getting-started/tutorials/beginner/): Small, single-peripheral SF32-SDK tutorials for right after your first hello_world flash — GPIO, shell, ADC/PWM basics.
- [Intermediate Tutorials](https://uForge.io/getting-started/tutorials/intermediate/): Middleware and combined workflows on SF32 — I2C sensors, graphical UI, BLE services, audio playback, and persistent storage.
- [Advanced Tutorials](https://uForge.io/getting-started/tutorials/advanced/): Shippable-product-level SF32 work — measured power, safe OTA, custom hardware bring-up, crash analysis, and multi-connection Bluetooth.

## Notes for AI agents and coding assistants

- All hardware design guides use numbered sections, tables, and figures (e.g. "Table 5.1-1", "Figure 5.2-3") scoped per H3 subsection; treat these numbers as stable anchors when quoting specific values.
- Each chip/module family follows the same structure: an Introduction page (device overview, variants, packages, applications) and a Hardware Design Guide (schematic guidance, PCB layout, manufacturing checklist); several chips also have a standalone Hardware Design Checklist page.
- This domain publishes English content only. A separate Chinese documentation set exists but is not part of this site's published content.
- For authoritative electrical specifications, pin mappings, and component qualification beyond what's summarized here, the guides link out to SiFli's datasheets, user manuals, and the SiFli Approved Vendor List.
